newsitem.title: UK: IEA sees extra oil supplies outstripping demand.
newsitem.headline: IEA sees extra oil supplies outstripping demand.

text.p: Extra oil supplies from non-OPEC producers will more than match strong growth in demand this year after delays in new oilfield projects helped world prices hit six year highs late last year, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
Non-OPEC countries would supply 45.5 million bpd this year, up from 43.5 million in 1996, the agency projected in its monthly Oil Market Report.

World demand was set to rise by 1.9 million bpd to 73.7 million bpd on top of growth in 1996 of 1.7 million bpd, the IEA said. The demand figure was 100,000 bpd higher than in the IEA's previous monthly report.

The agency maintained its projections for high non-OPEC supply growth despite making sharp 400,000 bpd downward revisions to its estimates for the fourth quarter of last year and the first quarter of 1997, to 44.2 million bpd and 45.2 million bpd respectively.
The reductions came as a result of weather related supply disruptions in Asia, delayed North Sea oilfield starts and slower-than-expected maintenance in several regions.
"Although some of the downward revisions have been carried forward to 1997, the net result is a slightly larger projected year-on-year growth in non-OPEC supply," the IEA said.
Oil prices have fallen this week as demand for winter heating oil slumped, taking benchmark British Brent blend down nearly a dollar since Friday to $21.75 a barrel for March futures.
The IEA said January world oil supplies rose 900,000 bpd to 74.76 million bpd from a revised December figures with non-OPEC adding 500,000 bpd and OPEC the remainder.
OPEC output at 26.9 million bpd was boosted by a 240,000 bpd increase from Iraq in its first full month of exports under the United Nations oil-for-food exchange.
Several other members outside the Gulf produced more in January, particularly in Nigeria and Venezuela, seen by the IEA and other observers as OPEC's biggest quota violator.
"The largest OPEC increase outside of the Persian Gulf occurred in Nigeria, where production rose by about 45,000 bpd," the IEA said.
Venezuelan production is estimated to have risen by a similar amount to almost 3.1 million bpd, against its OPEC quota of 2.359 million.
The agency revised down its December estimate for world supply by a huge 800,000 bpd to 73.83 million.

"Contributing to strong year end prices world oil supply ended 1996 with much less of a surge than had been anticipated as North Sea and Chinese offshore volumes were well below expectation," it said.
Oil company distillates stocks in Organisation of Cooperation and Development (OECD) countries were not drawn during December for the first month since 1990, the IEA.

Distillates stocks, which include vital winter heating oil, stood 12 million barrels higher than a year earlier following a 19 month period during which end of month stocks were consistently lower than a year before, the IEA said.
Total oil industry stocks fell by just 1.3 million barrels per day (bpd) in December which contrasts with a much faster 2.7 million bpd draw in December 1995.
